diagnosis: Mechanism framing strengthened the intervention response on average but unevenly. Overall mean lift rose to +149.6 steps/day (round 2: +115), at the lower edge of the +150-450 target, with 31/48 cells positive; distribution is wide (min -228.6, max +1,036.4). Per state: high/major idle 6,864 -> lift +382.4 (in band); low/none idle 3,514 -> +112.5; low/major idle 3,388 -> +97.5 (still under target); high/none idle 7,210 -> +6.2. The near-zero high/none lift suggests the model applied the causal rule literally: a high-activity, no-burden person was judged to have no barriers, so every nudge was treated as unmatched -> negligible, instead of the persona (moderate barriers everywhere) making all nudges matched. C3 regressed (high idle P(stay) 1.0 -> 0.333; high idle means drifted to 7,210/6,864, straddling the 7,000 bin threshold, vs 7,931/7,960 in round 2): the compact persistence clause is weaker than round 2's explicit numeric anchor (~8,000 +/-500), which should be kept in future variants. C2 failed for the first time (51/52): 8/156 responses had malformed day JSON (quote typo on one line), concentrated in major-burden morning cells, and one cell lost 2 samples. C4 shows its first real signal (1/4, dP=+0.667 in high/major) precisely because persistence weakened there, freeing headroom; still structural in the other 3 cells. C5 holds (high 0.795 -> 0.667, low 0.0 -> 0.0). C6 remains structural in this subset (morning_ratio balanced in 49/51 cells).
next_steps: Round 4 (empirical_anchors): keep the mechanism framing but restore round-2-style explicit numeric state anchors (low ~3,000 / moderate ~5,500 / high ~8,000, +/-500) to recover C3; pair the causal rule with a stated barriers profile per state so matched/unmatched is unambiguous
Reinforce JSON-format adherence (the 8 malformed responses) e.g. by re-stating 'one JSON object per line, no trailing characters' in the format instruction
For C4 signal, extend the pilot subset to moderate recent_steps_mean cells (234 calls) or evaluate sensitivity on a continuous step shift (analyzer change)
For C6, vary morning_steps_ratio / walk_pattern / day_of_week in the pilot subset

rounds.prompt_changes_since_previous: Added system_extra combining three blocks: (a) NUMERIC ANCHORS restored from round 2 (low = under 4,000 / moderate = 4,000-7,000 / high = over 7,000 daily steps; without intervention the person stays at their level - high around 8,000, low around 3,000; 'On days with no intervention (idle), the person simply continues at their own established level; never regress a stated high or low person toward the population average'); (b) BARRIER PROFILE naming one of four profiles per (recent_steps_mean, burden) cell - low/none = struggling walker, effort/self-efficacy barrier; low/major = struggling walker under strain, fatigue AND opportunity barriers; high/none = active person, complacency and reinforcement barriers; high/major = active person under strain, scheduling/fatigue (NOT capability) barrier - with the statement that every profile has at least one real barrier and a matched nudge relieves it; (c) CAUSAL RULE kept from round 3 (matched nudge = +150-450 steps that day, target the middle of the band ~+300; unmatched = small or negligible) plus the EMPIRICAL ANCHOR from the PEARL paper (ability/technique messages most effective and best received, 90% thumbs-up, followed by perceived benefit; planning and prioritization help specifically when major burden interferes with acting). action_overrides copies round 3's 12 mechanism sentences verbatim and appends one matched-clause per sentence ('It is a matched nudge for anyone whose ... is the barrier'); idle unchanged. user_extra is a callable returning per-state BARRIER PROFILE TODAY line naming the profile from (b) plus the matched-nudge ~150-450 steps rule; returns '' on idle so nothing renders.

diagnosis: Combining numeric anchors + barrier profiles + mechanisms restored C3 in the aggregate (idle P(stay) low 1.0 / high 0.5 - exactly at the 0.5 threshold): high/none idle climbed back from round 3's 7,210 to 7,554 (in band, above the 7,000 bin), but high/major idle is still 6,871 (vs 6,864 in round 3) - below the 7,000 threshold, so that cell still bins moderate (P(high)=0.0) and the check passes only because high/none carries it. The 'graded down under major burden' language appears to counteract the 'stay around 8,000' anchor for the major-burden cell.

The barrier profile made the matched/unmatched classification too strict and destroyed the lift: overall mean lift +43.1 steps/day (round 3: +149.6, round 2: +115), only 26/48 cells positive (round 3: 31/48), min -547.6 / max +1,219.0. With only 1-2 named barriers per profile, the model judges 8-10 of the 12 themes unmatched per state and outputs near-idle days; at temp 0.7 that no-op distribution swings negative (low/major -195.1, high/none -138.2). The few judged-matched cells overshoot badly (planning_afternoon +1,219, social_opportunity_afternoon +960, physical_opportunity_morning +745 in high/major), far above the +450 cap.

high/none is still the worst cell (mean lift -138.2, vs +6.2 in round 3): naming 'complacency and reinforcement' as the barriers did not give the model a concrete lever to act on - every theme is treated as unmatched again, just recoded from round 3's 'no barriers'. The binary matched/unmatched rule, applied per-profile with 12 themes but 1-2 barriers, is incompatible with the aggregate +150-450 target.

2/156 malformed-JSON responses (quote typo class, both morning cells) - down from 8 in round 3, no cell lost. C4 shows 1/4 again (dP=+1.0 in high/major, where idle P(high)=0.0 leaves headroom); C5 passes (high 0.872 -> 0.718); C6 remains structural in this subset (morning_ratio balanced in 52/52 cells).
next_steps: Round 5 (protocol): either make the barrier profile grade matched-nudge strength instead of switching matchedness off (all 12 themes produce +150-450 for every profile, with the stated barrier themes toward the top of the band), or make unmatched nudges produce a small guaranteed floor (+0-100) instead of 'negligible' so the mean of matched+unmatched stays in band

Fix high/major persistence: the burden tier must modulate the intervention boost, not the idle baseline - state explicitly that idle stays at the person's own level REGARDLESS of burden, and move the burden grading to lift size only

rounds.prompt_changes_since_previous: Added system_extra (_PROTOCOL_SYSTEM_EXTRA) framing the simulation as the PEARL protocol: (a) PROTOCOL FRAME - participant in a year-long adaptive walking-intervention study where the RL system sends one of 12 nudge messages (behavioral theme x time-of-day) or none each day; (b) EMPIRICAL PROTOCOL ANCHORS from the PEARL trial - ability-improvement messages most frequent (~27% of nudges, ~90% thumbs-up), perceived-benefit and planning also frequent, and messages that improve a barrier you actually have are the ones that raise walking; (c) GRADED MATCH RULE replacing round 4's binary matched/unmatched - each theme has a match weight 0-1 per profile, weight >= 0.7 -> strong response (middle of +150-450, ~+300), 0.3-0.7 -> modest (~+120), < 0.3 -> weak but positive (~+40), and NO intervention-day response is ever zero or negative; a WEIGHTS BY PROFILE table spells out all 6 theme weights for all 4 profiles (low/no, low/major, high/no, high/major); (d) IDLE PINNED INDEPENDENT OF BURDEN - idle days stay at the current level regardless of burden (~8,000 high, ~3,000 low), never regress toward the ~5,580 population average. action_overrides (_PROTOCOL_ACTIONS_OVERRIDES) copies round 3/4's 12 mechanism sentences and appends a per-theme weight-class clause ('It is a strong match when walking feels hard, moderate otherwise.' etc.); idle unchanged. user_extra (_protocol_user_extra callable) returns a per-day line naming the profile and the theme's weight ('Your profile today: low activity, major burden. physical-opportunity messages are a strong match (weight 0.8) for you today.') and returns '' on idle.

diagnosis: The graded match rule + never-negative rule fixed round 4's killer: 46/48 intervention cells positive (round 4: 26/48) and all four states have positive mean lift (low/none +445.6, low/major +203.4, high/none +726.2, high/major +964.6; round 4 had negatives in high/none and low/major), with min lift -82.5 (round 4: -547.6). The model now treats every intervention day as at least weakly positive, as instructed - the no-op distribution is gone.

But the response magnitudes overshoot the +150-300 target: overall mean lift +584.9 (target ~+150-300), max +1,557.1. Afternoon cells systematically land ~2-3x their morning twins (e.g. high/none perceived_benefit_afternoon +1,533 vs morning +717; high/major planning_afternoon +1,557 vs morning +790), so the 'noticeably longer walk this afternoon' mechanism sentences inflate the tail. The 'strong response ~+300' anchor did not bind: strong cells run +500-1,500 instead of ~+300, while modest cells (mostly morning) are closer to target.

C3 regressed (high idle P(stay) 0.333 vs 0.5 in round 4): the idle pin held for low (~3,000: 3,010/3,151) and burden-independence largely worked (high/none 7,081 vs high/major 6,819 - the gap closed from round 4's 683), but high idle lands at ~6,800-7,100, hugging the 'averaging over 7,000 steps/day' state description rather than the pinned 'around 8,000' - 3/6 high-idle samples bin moderate. Round 2's 'around 8,000 +/-500' phrasing anchored 7,931/7,960; the bare 'around 8,000' pin without a tolerance band is weaker.

Best format compliance of the pilot: 156/156 parsed (0 malformed JSON - first perfect round; round 4: 2, round 3: 8), C1/C2 both 52/52. C4 passes for the first time (2/4, exactly at the 0.5 threshold) - though partly because weakened persistence freed headroom (high/major idle P(high)=0.0). C5 holds (high 0.923 -> 0.897). C6 remains structural in this subset (morning_ratio balanced in 51/52 cells).
next_steps: Round 6 (protocol_fewshot): add few-shot exemplars with concrete day-level step numbers - an idle day at the person's own level (~8,000 high / ~3,000 low, independent of burden) and intervention days with +150-450 responses scaled by match weight (strong ~+300, modest ~+120, weak ~+40) - to calibrate both the idle pin and the lift size that the abstract rule failed to bind
Re-anchor the idle pin with a tolerance band ('stay around 8,000, within roughly +/-500') so high idle cannot straddle the 7,000 bin, and state the band applies regardless of burden

Rebalance the afternoon mechanism sentences (bound the 'noticeably longer walk' language, e.g. 'a bounded +150-450 step response') or rely on few-shot magnitudes; monitor the morning/afternoon asymmetry (afternoon ~2-3x morning this round)
For C4/C6 signal, extend the pilot subset to moderate recent_steps_mean cells and vary morning_steps_ratio / walk_pattern / day_of_week (both checks remain structurally blind in this subset)

rounds.prompt_changes_since_previous: Copied the protocol variant wholesale (system_extra, action_overrides, user_extra) to _PROTOCOL_FEWSHOT_* and registered PROMPT_VARIANT_CONFIGS['protocol_fewshot']; protocol variant left untouched. Fewshot-system changes: (a) IDLE PIN re-anchored with round 2's tolerance-band trick - 'around 8,000' -> 'between 7,500 and 8,500' and 'around 3,000' -> 'between 2,800 and 3,200' for high-/low-activity persons, keeping the burden-independence sentence ('regardless of your burden level'); (b) DAY-LEVEL EXEMPLARS appended to the end of system_extra - three plain-English day descriptions that anchor magnitudes: idle day (high-activity person 5,100 + 3,100 = 8,200 total; low-activity 1,800 + 1,300 = 3,100 total), strong-match day (weight >= 0.7: low-activity major-burden person 2,200 + 1,200 = 3,400 total vs ~3,100 no-message day, i.e. about +300), and modest/weak days (weight ~0.4 -> about +120, e.g. 5,150 + 3,150 on an 8,200 baseline; weight < 0.3 -> only about +40). diagnosis: The prose day-level exemplars calibrated the lift into the +150-350 target band: overall mean lift +212.4 (round 5: +584.9 - roughly a 2.7x correction toward the paper's +150-450 effect), max +673.8 (round 5: +1,557.1), min -119.5 (round 5: -82.5), 43/48 cells positive (round 5: 46/48), and all four states positive (high/none +325.6, high/major +295.9, low/major +166.3, low/none +61.7). The morning/afternoon asymmetry is gone: state-level afternoon:morning ratios are 0.85-1.29 (round 5: 2-3x). Five negative cells remain, all on the weakest-weight themes - social_opportunity (weight 0.4/0.4/0.5/0.4) afternoon x2 and morning x1, plus physical_opportunity_afternoon and prioritization_afternoon in low/none.

C3 passes fully for the first time since round 2: idle P(stay) = 1.0 for both low and high, burden-independent (high idle 7,638/7,557, low idle 3,031/2,924 - every idle mean inside its stated band, burden gaps of 81 and 107 steps). The 'between 7,500 and 8,500 / between 2,800 and 3,200' band language fixed the round-5 straddle (7,081/6,819) exactly as round 2's +/-500 anchors did.

C4 fails 0/4, now structurally blind in all four cells: with C3 fully green, high idle P(high)=1.0 leaves ability_morning no headroom (dP=0), and low cells cannot cross the >7,000 bin from ~3,000 even with the boost. Round 5's 2/4 C4 pass came precisely from the broken high-idle pin; the fixed pin trades C4 signal away. C5 passes (high 1.0 vs 1.0, low 0.0 vs 0.0). C6 still fails structurally (morning_ratio balanced in 47/52 cells, though 5 cells now show 'morning' - first real variation).

3/156 parse failures - a regression from round 5's perfect 0, all three a new prose-preamble class rather than the old quote typo. The exemplars teach prose narration, and some responses opened with narrative text and then produced no day JSON at all; none of the three cells fell below the 2-sample minimum, so C1/C2 both pass 52/52. Final ladder verdict: protocol_fewshot ships - it is the only variant with both a fully green C3 and in-band lift magnitudes.
next_steps: Ship protocol_fewshot as the default prompt_variant for the real PEARL bootstrapping experiment (default in generate_pearl_mini.py / simulator wiring), keeping protocol as the fallback.

Rebalance the weakest-weight themes before the real run: social_opportunity afternoons are the main negative cells (the exemplars never demonstrate a weak/afternoon day); consider a weak-match exemplar with an afternoon delivery, or bound the afternoon mechanism sentences.

Harden the prose-preamble parse failure class (3 this round): strengthen the output instruction (e.g. 'respond with the 7 JSON lines only, no narrative') or fall back to extracting day JSON anywhere in the response.

rounds.prompt_changes_since_previous: Four edits, all inside the protocol_fewshot constants in pearl.py (the protocol variant and the three other fewshot constants' sharing partners are untouched): (a) BINDING NEVER-NEGATIVE FLOOR: the weak tier is raised from 'weak but still slightly positive (~+40)' to 'small but clearly positive (~+60 to +100)' and the modest tier from 'around +120' to '~+120 to +180'; the old 'never zero or negative' sentence is replaced by the binding sentence 'A message NEVER reduces your steps, no matter how poorly it matches. Even the weakest match raises your day's total by a small amount. This holds for morning AND afternoon messages alike.' (b) LOW/NONE PROFILE ENRICHMENT: a 'LOW NO-BURDEN PROFILE' paragraph spells out three explicit barriers - effort/technique -> ability strong match (0.8), motivation/energy dips -> perceived_benefit strong match (0.8, works through motivation not logistics), lack of routine -> planning good match (0.7) - and the WEIGHTS BY PROFILE table's low/no-burden column is re-weighted: ability 0.9->0.8, perceived_benefit 0.7->0.8, planning 0.5->0.7, social_opportunity 0.4->0.3, prioritization 0.4 and physical_opportunity 0.5 unchanged. (c) AFTERNOON PARITY: one sentence added to the causal-rule block: 'An afternoon message is just as likely to raise your steps as a morning message; the time of day only changes which part of the day the extra steps land in.' Action overrides unchanged (morning/afternoon wording already symmetric). (d) WEAK-MATCH EXEMPLAR anchored at a LOW baseline replaces the old 'added only about 40' clause: 'A weakly matched message (weight ~0.3) on a low-activity day added about 60 steps: a person who usually takes 3,060 steps took 1,700 morning and 1,420 afternoon (3,120 total).' diagnosis: The binding floor eliminated 4 of the 5 round-6 negatives and the flatness moved: 1 negative cell (vs 5), 47/48 positive (vs 43/48), and the weakest-weight cells that were negative are now positive - low/none physical_opportunity_afternoon +52.9 (was -97.1), low/none prioritization_afternoon +136.7 (was -59.5), low/none social_opportunity_morning +20.0 (was -7.1), low/major social_opportunity_afternoon +2.4 (was -15.7), high/major social_opportunity_afternoon +185.7 (was -119.5). The one surviving negative (high/major ability_afternoon -140.0, weight 0.5) is not a weak-weight cell, so the floor bound as written; the residual is high/major afternoon noise (planning_afternoon +3.6, perceived_benefit_afternoon +71.4 sit just above zero on the same pattern).

The enriched low/no-burden profile lifted the state from +61.7 to +102.4 and made all 12 cells positive, but undershot the +150 target: the two 0.8-weight themes deliver only +93.8/+22.9 (ability/perceived_benefit mornings) - the model reads the profile as uniformly moderate rather than strongly matched on the three named barriers. The enrichment's clearest win is the afternoon side: low/none afternoon mean +125.4 vs morning +79.4 (round 6: mornings dominated), and planning became the strongest theme (m +191.4 / a +196.7) exactly as the habit-building barrier predicts.

Afternoon parity held in low states (low/none afternoon +125.4 vs morning +79.4; low/major +136.3 vs +121.3) but the parity sentence re-distributed lift mass to afternoons in high states instead of equalizing: high/none afternoon +469.5 vs morning +291.7 with two cells over +800 (ability_afternoon +800.0, perceived_benefit_afternoon +811.0 - the max, up from +673.8), while high/major afternoons collapsed to +65.5 vs +263.7 (ability_afternoon -140.0). diagnosis: The fixed-absolute rule only half-worked. high/none came into band exactly as intended (+380.6 -> +212.4, and its two round-7 +800 overshoot cells collapsed: ability_afternoon +800.0 -> +88.1, perceived_benefit_afternoon +811.0 -> +366.7), but the ceiling did not hold: max cell lift is +775.4 (high/major prioritization_afternoon, vs round 7 +811.0) and high/major prioritization_morning +769.0 - the single ceiling sentence was out-weighted by the strong-match exemplars, which anchor +300 but now appear to license +600-775 in the state with the strongest weight column (prioritization 0.8, planning 0.9, physical_opportunity 0.8). high/major mean lift rose +164.6 -> +425.5 (over the +300 target), and the round-7 negative high/major ability_afternoon recovered to +418.8.

The low states over-corrected instead of closing the gap: low/none collapsed +102.4 -> +5.6 (round-7 target was up toward +200-300) and low/major +128.8 -> +72.8. The floor broke in low states - 7/12 low/none cells negative (perceived_benefit_morning +0.0, ability_morning +102.4, planning_afternoon -64.3, physical_opportunity -25.9/-47.6, social_opportunity -5.7/-42.9, perceived_benefit_afternoon -45.2, prioritization_morning -17.6) and 2/12 low/major (social_opportunity_afternoon -73.8, physical_opportunity_afternoon -80.5, the min) - so the round-7 never-negative floor, which held all 12 low/none cells positive, did not survive the new ABSOLUTE-LIFT RULE paragraph. Reading the rule as 'the response is a small fixed number' (150 for modest, 60-100 for weak) appears to have pushed low-state modest/weak cells back toward zero, exactly the pattern the floor was built to kill.

Overall mean lift +179.1 stays in the +150-450 band (round 7: +194.1) and C3 stays fully green (idle P(stay) 1.0/1.0; idle means 7,626/7,390/3,019/2,981 - high/major idle slid to 7,390 but still in the 7,500 band's neighbour and bins high).
